correctness.rationale: Fourier inverse uses the assumed roots and characteristic. For any ideal vector with nonzero coordinate alpha, multiplication by a coordinate delta extracts delta at Phi^{-1}(alpha). Separate left/right multipliers propagate this basis vector through Phi^{-1} and Psi^{-1}, and finiteness recovers alpha and the entire H orbit. Every orbit-span is a two-sided ideal; cross-orbit products vanish and every delta_chi is delta_{Phi chi}*delta_{Psi chi}. The simple-block lattice follows without extrapolation. Exact program checks eight cyclic dihedral examples, one different Alexander map, C3xC3 and all 116 subspaces of F7[R3].

originality.rationale: A complete two-sided ideal lattice and simple two-sided-block classification are not stated by inspected prior Fourier multiplication, one-sided decomposition, or augmentation-powers results. Ta 2026, Proposition 5.1 supplies the product identity but requires a further coordinate extraction and independent orbit-propagation argument. EFT 2018 Proposition 4.18 and Kaur–Singh 2023/2024 give right ideals and representation constituents, which do not directly give this two-sided lattice, and earlier source coverage is acknowledged. Searches of published mathematical records by invariant and dual-orbit parameter found no equivalent claim. Residual risk: general nonassociative ideal results or an implicit reduction via representation theory not located.
residual_risks: General theorems about nonassociative algebra ideals or modular representations could imply the orbit lattice in an unrecognized formulation.

value.rationale: The two-sided ideal lattice of an entire natural nonassociative algebra family is a complete and usable structural invariant, recovering all simple two-sided blocks, their dimensions, orthogonality and the exact number of ideals. It distinguishes right-irreducible module decompositions from genuine two-sided simplicity, with an arithmetic count for the standard dihedral family; neither a parameter renaming nor a single small example.
